answer.rationale: Memory 57 is strongest because it explicitly reports qualified revenue gains and no measurable retention harm, directly addressing both revenue quality and sustainability. Memories 31, 86, and 91 show leading indicators—activation, adoption, engagement, and meaningful-action completion—but omit downstream conversion, retention, and revenue outcomes. Memory 44 supports pipeline quality for enterprise sales-assisted flows but does not report closed-won revenue or retention. Memory 73 reports acquisition and revenue lift for price-sensitive SMBs, but omits durability, retention, margin, and qualification effects; aggressive promotional pricing may also pose sustainability risk. Memory 91 is least supported because week-one engagement and first meaningful action are especially indirect proxies for long-term qualified revenue.
